subject: RE: BrightCo MSA & Order Form — Productization/Training Redlines
message_1_body:
Hi Hannah,

Thanks for taking this to legal. Attached are our redlines to the MSA and Order Form. The key points we need sign-off on from our side: 

- BrightCo must retain all title to outputs and derived works that are incorporated into our products (we're asking for explicit output ownership).
- No use of customer data or outputs to train or tune Redwood models without an explicit opt-in in the Order Form.
- Any telemetry or logs used by Redwood must be confined to operational monitoring and not used to improve models for commercial productization.

We flagged language in Section 5 and in the Order Form that we think leaves the door open to Redwood using outputs for broader training — that won't work for us. We prefer an explicit carve-out: model training = opt-in only.

Can your team confirm whether Redwood can accept the attached redlines or propose narrowly tailored alternative language? Also happy to schedule 30 minutes tomorrow if it helps.

Thanks,
Sophia Li
Head of Procurement, BrightCo

Attachments: BrightCo_MSA_redlines_20280322.docx, OrderForm-v3_redline.pdf
message_2_subject: RE: MSA redlines: productization + training carve-outs
message_2_body:
Sophia — thanks for the redlines and the clear summary.

Quick acknowledgement: we received the doc and Jordan/Naomi are looped in for legal and commercial tradeoffs. A couple of framing points from our side before Jordan proposes precise language: 

> BrightCo: 'No use of customer data or outputs to train or tune Redwood models without explicit opt-in.'

We agree on the principle that training should be opt-in. Our concern is operational telemetry (latency, failed requests, safety signals) and short-lived KV cache or prefix traces that we use to diagnose and improve service reliability. If the MSA disallows any secondary use of any signal, it breaks our ability to operate the service at scale.

Proposed compromise (high-level):
- Customers keep title to outputs and can grant a separate, explicit 'productization license' in the Order Form if they want Redwood to build product features from outputs.
- Redwood may use aggregated and de-identified telemetry and quality feedback to improve the hosted service and model-serving safety, but we will not use customer content or raw outputs to retrain public commercial models unless the customer explicitly opts in in the Order Form.
- For customers that require stronger guarantees, offer a dedicated model variant or a private deployment (VPC/on-prem) and an option for a contractual audit of telemetry handling.

Jordan/Naomi — can you draft concrete redline language that reflects the above and addresses: scope of 'aggregated/de-identified telemetry', permitted operational uses, and an opt-in path for training/productization? Also note BrightCo asked for output ownership wording; we should keep that but ensure it doesn't preclude the productization license option.

Happy to hop on a call with BrightCo once we have a short counter.

Best,
Hannah
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

message_3_subject: Re: MSA redlines: proposed legal language
message_3_body:
Team / Sophia — I reviewed BrightCo's redlines and drafted a compact counterproposal that should address their commercial concerns while preserving Redwood's ability to operate and improve the service. Key elements below and attached in-line redline (see OrderForm-Redwood-Counter.docx).

1) Output ownership: add a sentence to Section 3 (Customer Outputs) — 'Customer retains ownership of Outputs it receives from the Service. Provider (Redwood) shall have no ownership rights in Customer Outputs except as expressly granted in an Order Form.' This preserves customer title while enabling an opt-in license.

2) Training and feedback license: new Section X — 'Use of Customer Materials for Model Improvement' with core bullets: 
   a) 'Provider will not use Customer Materials (including Outputs) to train or improve Provider's models for commercial productization without an explicit, written opt-in in an Order Form.'
   b) 'Provider may collect and use aggregated, de-identified telemetry and usage metrics solely to operate, maintain and improve the Service, provided such data cannot be re-associated with Customer or end users.'
   c) 'If Customer elects to permit Provider training on Customer Materials, the scope, duration, and compensation will be set forth in the Order Form and may include additional safeguards (e.g., data minimization, deletion schedule, and audit rights).'

3) Operational carve-outs: clarify that short-lived caching, KV-store metadata, runtime safety logs and error traces used for debugging are not "training" where retained only for operational troubleshooting and are subject to retention limits.

4) Productization/competitive use: propose language limiting Provider from productizing specific customer Outputs into features that materially replicate Customer products unless Customer has granted a productization license in the Order Form.

5) Audit and compliance: include an option for customers to request a one-time review/audit of telemetry handling (reasonable notice and mutually agreed scope).

I tried to keep the wording surgical; the counter redline also includes a short glossary to define 'Customer Materials', 'Outputs', and 'Aggregated Telemetry'.

Sophia — materially, if BrightCo accepts (1) customer retains output title, (2) training requires an opt-in order form, and (3) Redwood can use aggregated telemetry for ops, this should meet most procurement risk bars while keeping the service viable. Happy to walk through line-by-line.

Jordan Blake
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

message_4_subject: BrightCo MSA — Redwood counterproposal and next steps
message_4_body:
Sophia — attaching Redwood's counter redline (OrderForm-Redwood-Counter.docx). Summary of what we are proposing and the requested confirmations we need from BrightCo: 

Summary of counter (short):
- BrightCo keeps ownership of Outputs (we add explicit clause).
- Training on Customer Materials: prohibited unless Customer opts in via Order Form.
- Aggregated/de-identified telemetry permitted for service ops and measured product quality improvements; we define strict de-identification and retention windows.
- Productization: Customer may grant a productization license in the Order Form; absent that license Redwood will not transform Outputs into commercial features that materially replicate Customer products.
- Operational telemetry carve-outs and an audit option for customers with specific compliance needs.

Requested confirmations from BrightCo: 
1) Can you accept the concept of an explicit 'opt-in' in the Order Form for training/productization? If so, we will add a short Order Form checkbox and sample pricing language.
2) Is BrightCo comfortable with Redwood's use of 'aggregated, de-identified telemetry' for service operations? We included a 90-day retention cap for such telemetry in the redline — please flag if you need a shorter window.
3) If BrightCo requires full prohibition on telemetry beyond strictly necessary logs, would you be open to the dedicated/private deployment option as an alternative (we can provide an indicative cost uplift)?

Next steps / proposed timeline:
- Please review attached counter by end of day Friday.
- If BrightCo can accept the opt-in framework and the telemetry definition, we will prepare a short Order Form addendum for signature.
- If not, propose a 30-minute call next Tuesday 10:00–10:30 PT to walk line-by-line.

Thanks — Jordan and Naomi are on thread for any legal/commercial follow-ups.

Best regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: OrderForm-Redwood-Counter.docx
